title: Free lining caught in a zip and leave the zip working
instruction: Free the yellow lining caught in the washbag zip without tearing it. Check the zip moves past the snag, then let go.
context: Freeing a fabric snag requires easing the lining out while controlling the slider; pulling harder can damage the lining or zip.
setup: A 300 x 280 x 36 mm fabric washbag contains two sealed 500 g rice pouches, one each side of its 200 mm nylon-coil zip. The slider is 10 x 13 mm with an 8 x 25 mm pull tab. A 140 x 60 x 0.4 mm yellow woven-polyester lining flap is sewn at its two remote corners. Its free edge is caught 6 ± 1 mm into the slider’s left entrance. README.md specifies pouch placement, stitching and the measured snag/reset check; the fixed layout matches the setup image.
scoring: 1.0: lining free and intact, slider has moved at least 25 mm below and 45 mm above the original snag after the lining is eased clear, and both hands released for 2 seconds. 0.75 for that functioning zip while still held. 0.5 for freed intact lining before the travel check. Otherwise 0; lining or zip damage overrides all credit.
fidelity: Native YAM arms/cameras; flexible lining uses mass points with stretch and gravity. The slider is constrained to its sewn track. A tapered entrance compresses trapped cloth and creates finite friction; reversing unloads it. Grips are idealized. The weighted bag/track stay fixed. Teeth, tearing and friction use reduced rules; forces are uncalibrated. No phase-triggered release.
reset_notes: Use the same dry bag, 1,000 ± 10 g total contents and undamaged lining. Restore the slider mark and 6 ± 1 mm caught depth. Accept the reset only if a 2 N forward pull for 2 seconds moves the slider at most 2 mm, and reversing 5 mm needs at most 2 N. Recreate and recheck the snag after this test. Full preparation and rejection rules are in README.md.
